# Native CodeQL extraction

This workflow analyzes Actions, C/C++, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python and Rust on pull requests to `main`, pushes to `main`, a weekly schedule and manual dispatch. It keeps the default security query suites and remote threat model. There are no event path filters or security query exclusions. C/C++ uses real manual compilation; the other four analyses use their existing no-build modes.

`build.py` binds inputs to the checked-out commit on every run. It discovers package `src/*.c`, `.h` and `.inc` files dynamically and uses the package's unchanged configuration, R build flags and Rust archive. Rust dependencies are built offline before CodeQL tracing begins. The subsequent traced phase compiles every package C unit, the maintained standalone probes and the R test fixtures using their real includes. Current source hashes, compiler commands, installed R headers and generated probe-header mappings are retained with the coverage evidence. Generated instrumented headers are identified as derived inputs; they do not count as original production-header bodies.

`native-source-scope.json` lists the maintained standalone build inputs and 160 immutable historical C/header snapshots. The snapshots are archived benchmark data under the explicit manual-build policy. Their original classifications and publication bindings remain recorded. Every tracked C/C++/header/include path must be a discovered package input, a mapped maintained input or an unchanged historical snapshot. Unknown inputs, changed archived bytes and symlinks fail validation. A newly maintained standalone source needs a build route in the same reviewed change. Adding a package C source includes it automatically in the R build.

`collector.py` checks actual manual compilation records, source/header metrics, original-path function bodies, real R and descriptor type witnesses, extraction errors and reachable includes. It rejects archived headers reaching a maintained translation unit and unexpected traced dependency C units. The declaration-only `probe-bracket-live-cache.h` has explicit include, declaration and type checks. These checks cover the Linux LP64 build with R 4.6.0 and Rust 1.98.0. They do not establish every preprocessor branch, Windows or Apple-specific bodies, or full semantic equivalence of the extracted model.

The earlier 116-file no-build coverage contract failed and remains failed. Successful security-query evaluation alone did not prove acceptable extraction. The current manual active-source contract is a separately reviewed replacement for production coverage; its verdict and all five security jobs must succeed before merge.

Both CodeQL actions are pinned to `2892aa5e19bbd11bc0cff5427e3b750a04d9e3c2`. C/C++ additionally verifies the official CLI 2.27.1 Linux bundle and the 61 bundled `cpp-queries` 1.9.0 queries. Its initial evaluator setting is exactly one `--max-disk-cache=32768`, supplied through the pinned action's `CODEQL_ACTION_EXTRA_OPTIONS` implementation. This bounds the intermediate query cache, not total job storage or RAM. The collector verifies the actual run-queries and evaluator commands, completed query ledger and result files. The 32 GiB setting must be demonstrated by the actual production run; source checks and extraction-only qualification do not prove it will complete.

Keep action and bundle updates current through reviewed changes. Update both action pins, the narrowly approved action allowlist entries, the official bundle digest and query inventory together. Revalidate the command-option seam and coverage witnesses when the pinned action or CLI changes. Interface changes that affect the named type witnesses update those witnesses in the same PR.

GitHub rejects advanced CodeQL uploads while managed default setup is enabled. The reviewed rollout must replace managed setup with this workflow, preserve existing results and protections, and verify actual uploads for all five categories. If rollout fails, restore the captured managed setup and suspend the replacement workflow while diagnosing it. The private transition receipt records the exact settings request and rollback checks.

Deployment files: `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `.github/codeql/{build.py,collector.py,cpp.yml,native-source-scope.json,expected-query-names.json,README.md}` and `.github/codeql/queries/{qlpack.yml,diagnostics.ql,compilations.ql,includes.ql,files.ql,bodies.ql,includes-absolute.ql,types.ql}`. Private adaptation scripts, tests, replay receipts and rollout metadata are not deployment files.

Primary references: [workflow configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-scanning/workflow-configuration-options), [default-setup upload restriction](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-scanning/sarif-files/troubleshoot-sarif-uploads/default-setup-enabled), and [default-setup REST configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning#update-a-code-scanning-default-setup-configuration).
